headline: Committee sends housing project to Planning Commission, recommends farm notice measure

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: After testimony for and against, the committee recommended sending a housing and business project's plan and zoning changes to the Planning Commission. It also recommended adopting Resolution 26-68, on farm tenant notice before subdividing, on a 5–2 roll call vote.
meeting.recap: Some testifiers opposed the project, citing Pāʻia's small-town character.[[0:12:33]] Other testifiers supported it, saying Maui is in a housing crisis.[[0:22:51]] One testifier asked the committee to require more community meetings in Pāʻia first.[[0:41:33]] Resolution 26-84 would send Pāʻia community plan and zoning changes for over 40 acres to the Maui Planning Commission.[[0:52:47]] The project team said the plan includes a public parking lot of about 200 stalls.[[1:06:44]] The plan also includes about 170 homes: 120 single-family and 50 multi-family.[[1:07:54]] The applicant's attorney said 34 workforce rental units would stay affordable in perpetuity, meaning forever.[[1:14:41]] The planning director said council-started projects get less review, which could reduce community input.[[1:17:27]] Resolution 26-68 would send all three planning commissions a bill requiring farm landowners to notify tenants before subdividing.[[2:18:26]] The committee recommended adopting it on a 5–2 roll call vote.[[2:41:54]] That bill would allow at least two accessory dwelling units, or extra homes, on residential lots.[[2:43:00]]
meeting.next: A member asked the project team to keep a schedule of open community meetings to share when the item returns.

issues.oneLine: The committee recommended sending a Pāʻia housing and business project's plan and zoning changes to the Planning Commission.
issues.why: A supporter said Maui is in a housing crisis, and the project would add homes.
issues.next: The resolution goes next to the Planning Commission.
issues.brief: The plan includes about 170 homes: 120 single-family and 50 multi-family.[[#1]] Workforce rentals would serve households earning up to 120 percent of the area median income.[[#2]] Gap group homes for sale would target households between 120 and 220 percent of the area median income.[[#3]] A market study recommended pricing the market homes at $1 million to $1.6 million.[[#4]]
